findings.title: Order #1042 (Northstar Weekender Pack, $100.00 paid) can be paid out twice: a $30 price-adjustment refund and a full $100 refund can both be collected on the same order

evidence.summary: The order detail page treats cancellation, refund, and price adjustment as one mutually-exclusive group ('Price protection is not available while another order request is active'). The server correctly implements this in two of the three directions: completing a refund or a cancellation both disable price adjustment AND each other. But completing a price adjustment ($30 returned) leaves 'Request refund' fully clickable and availableActions.requestRefund = true. Chaining POST /api/order/price-adjustment -> POST /api/order/refund/request -> POST /api/order/refund/complete on the same order is expected to leave totalReturned = 30 + 100 = 130, exceeding the $100 the customer actually paid — a $30 overpayment to the customer (or, viewed the other way, a business logic hole that lets any customer claim 130% of their order value).
